newsitem.title: USA: Itron off 25 percent on latest disappointment.
newsitem.headline: Itron off 25 percent on latest disappointment.

text.p: The stock of Itron Inc., a maker of automatic utility meters, fell 25 percent Wednesday after the company reported a quarterly loss and issued the latest in a series of warnings about its business.
Itron was off $5.125 at $15.125 in Nasdaq trading after the Spokane, Wash.-based company, which peaked at $60 a share in April, disappointed Wall Street for the third time this year.
Late Tuesday Itron reported a loss of $4.5 million, or 34 cents per share, in the third quarter, compared with net income of $2.1 million, or 16 cents per share, a year earlier.
While the company had warned of the loss last month, executives told analysts in a conference call that the weakness would continue into the current quarter.

Analysts also were alarmed by news that the company had used up $55 million in cash over the past nine months and that it was scrapping nearly $3 million worth of hardware to allow an upgrade, said Michael Shea of Hancock Institutional Equity Services.
"Management has not shown any urgency to cut expenses and has shown little interest in earnings for the foreseeable future," he said. "People don't like to hear that on Wall Street."

He and other analysts said utilities have been slower than expected to adopt Itron's automatic meter reading systems, which would virtually eliminate the need for utility employees to go into neighbourhoods to read meters.
Itron's stock fell more than 25 percent after its September warning, and the stock fell 30 percent in late May after a similar warning.
